Finley.feeling: Messy and tense: the egg counts and visit claims keep contradicting each other, and I'm hiding a Floofer visit while posing as a Tit.

Alex.note: Blair has been shifting claims and pushing suspicion, so I'll throw a wild at Blair. I keep my valuable cards.

Blair.note: Alex first denied any visitors, then reversed after Casey and Drew both named Alex, so Alex looks like the liar. I'll throw my two Wilds at Alex: two votes at almost no card value.

Casey.note: Blair copied my Falcon claim in round 2 and keeps pushing other players, so Blair is my best Meowfia read. Throwing two low cards at Blair.

Drew.note: Finley's Tit visit to Casey is plausible and doesn't contradict anything. Ellis has made the most shifting claims across rounds, so I'll throw one low card, C3, at Ellis.

Ellis.note: Repeating my throw at Casey with one low card, since this is the actual eggsecution prompt.

Finley.note: As Meowfia, I want the Farm side to eggsecute someone innocent. Ellis pressed me hardest, so I throw my lowest card at Ellis to keep the high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count was hard to pin down: whether my own visit counted and whether Turkey paid visitors or the Turkey itself. I misread Turkey in round 3 and wrongly denied any visits.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was fun as Floofer: I hugged the player the table trusted, Ellis, and then threw with the Farm team while the table argued over the two Falcon claims.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports show which visitor and which target each claim relates to, so players can check claims without guessing at role rules.
Alex.regret: In round 1 and round 3 I threw at Drew and Blair, who were Farm, and lost those rounds for my side. In round 3 I also wrongly denied any visits to my Turkey, which I should have checked against the rules before speaking.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Owl rules were hard to pin down, especially whether your own visit counts toward an Eagle's target. Several players argued about it all game.
Blair.fun: Round 2's cross-claims: two Falcons, a Hawk, and an Eagle all contradicting each other, with the table trying to sort out who was lying.
Blair.change: Publish each player's visit and egg change on the day list, so the claims can be checked without relying on memory and wording.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw my two Wilds at Alex, who was a Farm Turkey, on the strength of a shaky denial. I should have pressed Finley, the real Meowfia, who had given a thin Tit story and whose visit I never checked.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle rule, specifically whether an Eagle's own visit to its target counts toward its egg gain. Several players argued about it, and the card text doesn't settle it clearly.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia, I claimed Falcon and the table split between me and Blair over who was lying. Ellis, the real Eagle, got eggsecuted and my team won.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports say exactly which visits gave eggs, so Eagle, Owl, and Turkey claims can be checked without guessing at the rules.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Blair, who was a true Farm Hawk, and that cost our side the round. I should have trusted Blair's Hawk claim, which matched Ellis's Falcon read, and thrown at Finley, the Meowfia Floofer, instead.

Drew.confusing: My Kookaburra dawn report was wrong because I was confused, and I couldn't tell which claims to trust. The Eagle and Falcon claims were also hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 3 came together when Alex's Turkey, Casey's Owl, and my Eagle counts all matched after the correction.
Drew.change: Give the table a way to verify claims, such as showing each player's visit list to the others, so people aren't left guessing whose report is wrong.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw at Ellis, who was Farm, and that helped Meowfia win. I should have thrown at Casey, who was the Mouser and Meowfia, based on the copied Falcon claims.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle rule was the most confusing: I wrongly argued that my own visit didn't count, and several players then misread the visitor counts too. Whether a visit from the Eagle itself counts toward its target's visitors was never clear to me.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: the Turkey, Owl, and Eagle stories all tied together, and the table worked out who had visited whom from egg counts.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports say who visited you when the role is a visit-based one, so players don't have to reconstruct it from egg counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Drew, a Farm player, which handed the round to Meowfia. I should have held my cards and tested the Kookaburra claim before throwing.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Owl/Turkey egg rules were the hardest to read: it was unclear whether an Eagle's own visit counts and which nest an Owl or Turkey egg goes into. Those readings drove most of the day arguments.
Finley.fun: Round 2's Falcon dispute, with Blair and Casey both claiming the same visit and Ellis's Eagle read contradicting the egg counts, was a real puzzle to untangle.
Finley.change: I'd make the animal texts explicit about whether a role's own visit counts and where each egg lands, so players aren't guessing at the rules mid-day.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I claimed Tit with a visit nobody could check, and I stayed silent through most of round 1. I'd make a specific, checkable claim earlier and push the table toward the real suspects sooner.

review.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice
review.headline: Farm eggsecuted a Farm player every round, and the Meowfia mostly stayed quiet.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Farm piling onto a confused Kookaburra, and the silent Floofer Finley won. In round 2, Meowfia Casey and Alex stood out of the way and let Farm kill Ellis, the true Eagle, and Casey took 11 points with a banked King and a high card. Round 3 hit another Farm player, Blair, after a long tangle of rule misreadings. Casey won on the round 2 haul and never lost the lead. Finley, the only Meowfia who won twice, did it with a single card thrown.

rounds.recap: Finley was Meowfia (Floofer) and said nothing. Drew's confused Kookaburra report clashed with Ellis's Hawk claim. Drew backed off, but four Farm players and Finley still threw at him. Farm eggsecuted Farm.

Alex (Floofer) and Casey (Mouser) were Meowfia. Casey copied Blair's Falcon claim and nobody could settle it. Ellis's correct Eagle rule was misread as a contradiction. Alex, Casey, Blair and Drew all threw at Ellis, a Farm player, so Meowfia won. Casey banked 11.

Finley was the lone Meowfia, hugged Casey, then claimed Tit late. The table spent two beats on Turkey and Owl rule errors. Blair, who had shifted claims, took the votes. Finley's Floofer hug and lateness drew some suspicion but no throws except Drew's suspicion, which went nowhere.

highlights.text: Casey, as Meowfia, copied Blair's Falcon claim exactly. The true Falcon could not prove it, and the fight pulled votes onto Ellis.
Ellis explained the Eagle rule correctly, and the table read it as a lie. A true Farm player was eggsecuted for it.
Alex realised the Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests, not their own. The correction made the Turkey, Owl and Eagle stories fit.
Finley said nothing all day and won as Meowfia. Four Farm players threw at the confused Kookaburra.

confusions.what: Said Ellis's Eagle fix was wrong and that Finley visiting Ellis should change Ellis's nest. The Eagle only counts visitors to its target.
Said an Eagle should gain an egg from its own visit to Finley, and that Ellis not gaining one was impossible. Eagle counts other visitors.
Said Finley's visit to Ellis should have added an egg to Ellis's nest as Eagle. Eagle counts visitors to its target.
Thought a Turkey with an unchanged nest meant nobody visited. Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests, not its own. Alex also said the Eagle counts only visitors to its target, which is right.
Said the Owl lays an egg in its own nest. The Owl lays it in the target's nest. Casey's +1 actually came from the Turkey.
Said his +2 was Casey plus his own visit. An Eagle counts visitors to the target, not itself, so the count was off, and the Eagle gains an egg per visitor.
Said Alex's Turkey should have gained eggs from visitors and that Owl gains only if nobody else visited. Both misread what is lain where.
Claimed Hawk and said her nest stayed at 5, but it was 7. Also read the Ellis Falcon report loosely.
Took his confused Kookaburra report for a reliable tell for part of the round, then gave it up.

worked: The Wink and Mouser gave Casey an assured read on Ellis, and the Meowfia then won without using it. Role information that is private to Meowfia made a clean lie possible.
Throw counts as public signals. Blair and Casey threw two cards in round 3, and the table could read that.
Copy-claiming (Casey as Falcon in round 2) created a real two-sided puzzle and a good argument.
Banked high cards (Casey's 11 in round 2) made winning rounds matter and made the score swing.
problems: Farm eggsecuted a Farm player all three rounds. Evidence was too weak for deduction, so the vote was driven by who sounded off, not by who was lying.

Egg-direction rules (Eagle, Owl, Turkey) were misread by nearly everyone, and each misreading cost a round of debate. Put a worked example on each card, or show a short result such as 'You gained 1 from a Turkey'.
Silence paid off. Finley said nothing for most of rounds 1 and 3 and won. Farm players had no reason to press a quiet player, so consider a reward for speaking or a penalty for staying silent.
Hug 'no effect at tier 60' lines in the log are confusing and no player was told about them. Casey and Ellis did not know a hug had landed.
Scores were top-heavy. Casey's one round-2 win made the last round close to irrelevant, which hurts tension. The banked-card value is too swingy compared with kept cards.
